_comment: GitHub branch ruleset for `main`, as an API payload. INERT until an
admin-scoped token applies it — see deploy/github/apply-branch-protection.sh.
This exists because `main` has NO protection today (OA-02 in
docs/OWNER_ACTION_AUDIT_2026-07-29.md confirms `"protected": false`),
and deploy.yml ships every push to main straight to production. So an
accidental direct push is an unreviewed path to the live site.
The second reason is subtler and is why `required_status_checks` matters
more than it looks: a PR with merge conflicts gets ZERO check runs,
because GitHub cannot build the merge ref. On the merge page that reads
identically to checks having passed. Requiring a check turns 'no checks'
from something that looks mergeable into something that cannot be merged.
`Validate PR` is the JOB name in pr-validation.yml, not the workflow name.
GitHub matches job names. The audit originally named `E2E Safety Net` and
`Deploy Production` here — both workflow names, neither of which would
ever match a check run.
Deliberately NOT required: `Boot stack + run journeys` (e2e.yml). It runs
only on PRs touching the shell/SSR paths, so requiring it would block
every PR that does not. And `Deploy To Production`, which only runs
post-merge and so can never be green pre-merge.
`required_approving_review_count: 0` is deliberate: this is a solo repo,
and requiring 1 approval means never being able to merge your own PR.
Zero still forces the PR path and still runs the check.
BYPASS ACTORS (stabilization audit 2026-10-07).  Applied as originally
written, this payload would have BLOCKED every legitimate automated
pusher to main and frozen production: the box timers
(deploy/dlf_fetch_and_push.sh, idpshow_fetch_and_push.sh,
playerctx_history_push.sh) push with the write deploy key, and
scheduled-refresh / refit-hill-curves / verify-sharp-production /
weekly-narratives push with GITHUB_TOKEN (GitHub Actions app 15368).
Deploy dispatch keys on those commits (CLAUDE.md W31-F001).  Both
credentials are therefore bypass actors.  Pinned by
tests/deploy/test_main_protection_ruleset.py, which fails if a new
direct-to-main pusher appears without a matching bypass actor.
ADMIN bypass_mode is `pull_request`, not `always`: the owner and every
AI agent session push as the SAME admin account, so `always` would give
any agent session direct-main authority.  `pull_request` blocks direct
pushes but still lets the admin merge a PR whose checks are red (the
emergency path: `gh pr merge --admin`).  Switching it to `always`
restores the owner's direct-push habit at the cost of the same power
for agents — an OWNER DECISION recorded in
docs/audit/STABILIZATION_2026-10-07.md (branch protection).
Residual risk: the Actions bypass covers ANY workflow with
`contents: write`.  Hardening follow-up: give the four bot pushers a
dedicated deploy-key secret and drop the Integration bypass.
name: main-protection
